newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bonds climbed slightly on Monday amid renewed optimism about the commitment of European countries to starting a single European currency in 1999 which helped the franc to erase last week's losses against the mark.
The December bond future was helped by the positive currency backdrop and also by spread related trades which traders said involved selling Bunds and buying the French bond contract.

Nevertheless, traders and analysts said the bond future looked destined to remain within a fairly narrow range this week, capped by resistance at 127.86 and 127.96 and supported at 127.52 and then 127.34-36.

"It looks like staying in a trading range with people looking for moments to buy on dips," Valerie Plagnol, economist at Credit Commercial de France, said. "But it's not the kind of week for any new highs."

Traders said the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday meant activity would start to wind down from Wednesday and that the French economic data due this week could send contradictory signals, both making any major market moves unlikely.
Analysts said while the French truck drivers strike had not yet had any marked impact on French assets it would need to be monitored closely for any moves to more widespread disruption.

"The lira re-entry boosted euro-optimism...and the dollar is up...both of which are positive for the currency," Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro in Paris, said. "Against this we have the truck drivers' strike."

"It's beginning to be an issue, it's in it's second week now and the truck drivers look determined," he said. "It's a potential threat, but it's not as important as the public sector strike last year."
Plagnol said "It doesn't look like the kind of strike that can really spread out...but there is a social risk which could affect the OAT/Bund spread."

Five French rail unions called jointly on Monday for their members to support the truck drivers "in the way they will judge necessary". The Communist-led CGT signed the joint declaration but called separately for a day of demonstration at the road blockades on November 27. Neither statement called for strikes.

The Bank of France left its intervention rate unchanged at Monday's money market tender. Some economists were still holding out for an intervention rate cut after Thursday's monetary policy council meeting although most expected no action.
"The franc's not brilliant, there's no reason to do it now, they'll probably do it at a more useful time," a trader said.

Most economists expected French October household spending on manfactured goods to show some slight weakness with the figures affected by the expiry of a government incentive scheme for car buyers at the end of September.

They said, however, consumer spending figures have been erratic during the past few months and a surprise was not out of the question given the difficulty of accounting for distortions to other spending from the incentive scheme.
The figures will be released at 0750 GMT by national statistics institute INSEE. Spending fell 1.5 percent in September.
